subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Do the secops and workflow owners accept these 14 upstream action revisions for the repository’s secret-, token-, publishing-, scanning-, Docker-, and Codex-enabled workflows after direct Codex contract verification?
rationale: CI can validate syntax and observed workflow execution, but it cannot decide trust in newly pinned third-party executable bundles or waive the repository’s direct Codex dependency-inspection gate.

options.title: Approve after boundary review
options.body: Verify the upstream revisions and sibling Codex permission contract, refresh the branch, and merge when the exact-head checks finish successfully.

options.title: Split highest-risk actions
options.body: Land low-privilege setup actions separately and hold the Codex, token, Docker login/publish, CodeQL, and automation pins for narrower owner review.

options.title: Keep current pins
options.body: Decline this grouped update and retain the existing immutable revisions until a smaller or better-proven dependency update is available.

recommendation.title: Approve after boundary review
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream revisions and sibling Codex permission contract, refresh the branch, and merge when the exact-head checks finish successfully.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows sustained ownership of the affected agent and release workflows, and this PR explicitly notified that account.
